title: The kernel/cokernel homology edge of a left exact functor
statement: Let $C,D$ be abelian categories and let $F:C\to D$ be additive and preserve finite limits. For a short complex $S=(A\to B\to C)$, set $Z(S)=\ker(B\to C)$ and let $\pi_S:Z(S)\to H(S)$ be its cohomology quotient. Define $e_S:H(F(S))\to F(H(S))$ by descending the composite $Z(F(S))\simeq F(Z(S))\xrightarrow{F(\pi_S)}F(H(S))$ through the quotient by boundaries. Then $\pi_{F(S)}e_S$ is this composite, and the maps $e_S$ are natural in all morphisms of short complexes. This construction requires no preservation of cokernels.

proof.text: Preservation of the kernel fork supplies the cycle isomorphism. Cancelling its monic kernel inclusion proves naturality and identifies the mapped boundary map.

The composite of the mapped boundary with the proposed cycle-class map is zero. The cokernel universal property defines the edge, with the asserted cycle equation. Cancel the epic cycle quotient and use the naturality of cycles and homology quotients to prove naturality of the edge.
